Enantioselective Rhodium-Catalyzed Cycloisomerization of
1,5-Bis(allenes) to Access 1,2-cis-Ethynyl- and Vinyl-Substituted
Five-Membered (Hetero)Cycles
Farhad Panahi+, Marzieh Samadani+, Felix Bauer, and Bernhard Breit*
Abstract: In this study, an enantioselective Rh-catalyzed
cycloisomerization of 1,5-bis(allenes) to furnish 1,2-
cis-ethynyl- and vinyl-substituted five-membered (het-
ero)cycles in high yields and with excellent diastereo-
and enantioselectivity is presented. The possibility of
further functionalization to access different chiral cyclic
and bicyclic skeletons is provided by the two orthog-
onal functional groups (alkyne and alkene). We also
demonstrate the scalability of the reaction through a
gram-scale synthesis and illustrate the synthetic utility of
the resulting 1,2-cis-ethynyl- and vinyl-substituted cyclic
product via several transformations. The proposed reac-
tion mechanism is supported by both density functional
theory (DFT) calculations and control experiments.
Transition metal-catalyzed cyclization and cycloisomeriza-
tion of unsaturated compounds provide a powerful synthetic
approach to structurally complex (hetero)cyclic molecules
in an atom- and step-economic manner from simple
substrates.<sup>[1–7]</sup> Allenes are not only found in natural products,
they are also valuable substrates in organic synthesis.<sup>[8–17]</sup> The
involvement of two allene moieties results in an increased
chemical space, providing bis(allenes) which are a unique
platform for the creation of various (hetero)cyclic scaf-
folds via cyclization and cycloisomerization reactions. Hence,
bis(allenes) are substrates to generate molecular complexity
in a small number of steps (high step economy).<sup>[18–36]</sup>
Bis(allenes) are also relevant in the total synthesis of complex
molecules, for example in the synthesis of the antibiotic Ery-
thromycin a bis(allene) is the key intermediate (Figure 1a).<sup>[37]</sup>
In transition metal catalyzed cyclization of bis(allenes), three
different types of cyclometalated intermediates have been
reported as most probable intermediates (Figure 1b).<sup>[18]</sup> The
metal coordinative cyclization between both terminal double
bonds, both internal double bonds, and an internal double
bond and a terminal double bond form the intermediates I,
II, and III, respectively. However, there are reactions which
might involve other intermediates.<sup>[18,31]</sup> The metal catalyst,
the reaction conditions and the structure of starting material
can control the formation of each intermediate. Therefore, by
controlling the reaction conditions and the catalyst system,
it is possible to obtain different types of products using
the same bis(allene) substrate (Figure 1c).<sup>[18–36]</sup> Accordingly,
the huge potential of cycloisomerization reactions with
bis(allenes) could be further explored for the synthesis of

In a preliminary experiment, a 64% yield of cycloisomer-
ized product 2a was obtained with high diastereoselectivity
(>20:1) by subjecting bis(allene) 1a to a catalyst system
consisting of 5.0 mol% of [Rh(COD)Cl]<sub>2</sub> (COD  1,5-
cyclooctadiene), DPEPhos ligand (L , 12.0 mol%) and 2-
chloroacetic acid (50 mol%) in 1,2-dichloroethane (DCE)
solvent, with the reaction being conducted at a temperature of
60 °C (Table 1, entry 1). In addition to the target compound,
two distinct byproducts (3a&4a) were detected. Although
product 3a is observed here, product 4a has been the subject
of previous reports.<sup>[25,29]</sup> In order to improve the yield of the
desired product, various parameters and reaction conditions
were investigated (ESI, Tables S1–S4). In the absence of an
acid additive, no product formation was observed and the
starting material was reisolated (Table 1, entry 2).
To improve the yield of the desired cycloisomerized
product 2a, the choice of additive was found to be a crucial
determinant (ESI, Table S3). Besides 2-chloroacetic, digly-
colic and 2-bromoacetic acid exhibited particularly high yields
(Table 1, entries 3 and 4). In order to induce enantioselectivity,
various chiral ligands were screened (ESI, Table S1). The
JoSPOphos SL-J688-1 (L ) ligand was found to be the most
efficient ligand (Table 1, entry 5). However, a low yield of
product was obtained with the use of 2-chloroacetic acid,
and the by-products were prominent. Thus, the efficacy of
this ligand was evaluated in conjunction with other additives
(Table 1, entries 5–7). Using diglycolic acid, the isolated
yield of 2a was improved (42%), however enantiomeric
excess (ee) dropped to 50%. In addition, a significant amount
(35%) of byproducts (3a&4a) was formed (Table 1, entry
6). Interestingly, the use of 2-bromoacetic acid resulted in
the increased formation of 2a (50%) and a high ee of 89%,
with the almost elimination of the byproduct 4a (Table 1,
entry 7). Encouragingly, as the concentration was increased,
2a was obtained in 80% yield in 92% ee (Table 1, entry 8). No
advantage was observed when other JoSPOphos type ligands
\mathbf { ( L _ { 3 } } \& \mathbf { L _ { 4 } ) }
were used (Table 1, entries 9&10). Having identified
the optimum reaction conditions, we began to evaluate the
scope of this diastereo- and enantioselective Rh-catalyzed
cycloisomerization of bis(allenes) (Figure 2). The assignment
of the absolute configuration of the syn diastereomer was
confirmed by X-ray analysis of compound 2b and showed the
S,S configuration of the stereogenic centers (see ESI). The
reaction conditions were found to be well-tolerated by a vari-
ety of functional groups, including nitro (2b), trifluoromethyl
(2e), amide (2d,m), keto (2k,n) and nitrile (2o-q). The poly-
substituted pyrrolidine 2c was synthesized with a yield of 52%
and good enantioselectivity, albeit a dr of 45:42:13 for three
diastereomers. One of the diastereomers was separable using
column chromatography. This methodology was found to be
effective for substrates bearing heterocyclic moieties such
as thiophene (2f) and pyridine (2g). The N-amide protected
bis(allene) also yielded the cyclic product 2d in a good yield
and high enantioselectivity. Thus, we could synthesize a range
of chiral 3-ethynyl-4-vinylpyrrolidine derivatives (2a-i). Two
chiral spirocarbocycles (spiro[4.4]nonane) were synthesized
from indandione (2k) and fluorene (2l) with moderate yields
and high ee.<sup>[45,46]</sup> The application of a bis(allene) derived from
a medicinally relevant template like barbituric acid, required
the use of the DPEPhos ligand and has led to the successful
synthesis of the corresponding spiro compound (2m). A
spiro[4.5]decane diastereomer was isolated in a moderate
yield of 48% but with a low enantiomeric excess of 24% by
cycloisomerisation of a dihydronaphthalene-based bis(allene)
(2n). Some chiral polyfunctionalized cyclopentane derivatives
were successfully synthesized using 2-phenylacetonitrile (2o),
and malononitrile (2p,q) demonstrating the high potential
of this method for the synthesis of significant chiral five-
membered-ring carbocycles. A new chiral derivative of
Valdecoxib was synthesized in satisfactory yield and high ee
under optimized conditions (2r). This finding is significant
because it demonstrates the potential of biomimicry in the
design and manufacture of novel compounds with unique
properties.<sup>[47]</sup> We did not obtain the desired product under
optimized conditions using a bis(allene) derived from 3-
cyanobenzenesulfonamide, but by increasing the amount of
additive and concentration we obtained product 2j in 78%
yield, >20:1 dr and 97% ee. It seems that the product 2j
is the Markovnikov addition product of hydrogen bromide
to the corresponding product.<sup>[48]</sup> The Markovnikov addition
products for compounds 2k and 2o were also isolated.<sup>[49]</sup>
